item.text: I’m checking the life-chances lens from both directions: broad economic baseline, then concrete opportunity-building policies, then the main counterevidence around politicized or incomplete treatment. After that I’ll stop searching and synthesize claim-level items.

item.text:
Bottom line: mostly yes, but only moderately and unevenly. Biden’s 2024 record improved ordinary people’s life chances most clearly through a stronger labor market, lower inflation, cheaper health/education access, and place-based investment. The case is weaker where housing stayed expensive, student-debt relief looked partly electoral, and Gaza/campus-policing decisions undercut a clean life-chances reading. Some gains also reflect the inherited post-pandemic rebound and other constraints outside the White House.

Search gap: I did not find evidence of a single, across-the-board mobility breakthrough. The strongest case is instead cumulative: stronger labor markets, lower inflation, cheaper health and education access, and place-based investment improved chances for many people, especially lower-income and disadvantaged groups. The main limits are persistent housing costs, mixed attribution for macro gains, and serious negative cases in protest policing and Gaza accountability.
